name: Turkey Pesto Pasta with Kale
ingredients: Feta Cheese (Great Value crumbled): 7 oz (196 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the rotini in well salted water to just under done. Reserve a cup or two of the starchy water before you drain, because you will want it in a minute.
While the pasta cooks, brown the ground turkey in a large pot, breaking it into crumbles, with the garlic powder, salt, and black pepper, until it is cooked through to 165F.
Strip the kale off its stems and chop it, then stir it into the hot turkey and cook 3 minutes until it wilts and goes dark green.
Add the drained pasta to the pot with the turkey and kale and kill the heat.
Stir in the basil pesto off the heat, adding splashes of the reserved pasta water until the sauce loosens and coats every piece. Off the heat matters, since boiling pesto turns it dull and bitter.
Taste and adjust with salt and pepper, remembering that the feta coming next brings its own salt.
Move everything into your weighed pot and hold the feta back for the containers.

name: Turkey Picadillo Rice Bowls
ingredients: Green Olives: 2 tbsp pitted Spanish olives + 2 tbsp brine (110 g)
steps: Brown the ground turkey in a large skillet, breaking it up as it cooks.
Add the chopped onion and green peppers and cook until they soften.
Stir in the cumin, then the diced tomatoes and tomato paste.
Let it simmer 10 to 15 minutes so the flavors meld and the sauce thickens.
Serve the picadillo over cooked white rice.

name: Turkey Pozole Rojo
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Stem and seed the dried ancho and guajillo chiles, toast them in a dry skillet for about 30 seconds a side until they smell nutty, then cover them in hot water and soak 20 minutes.
Blend the softened chiles with some of their soaking water, a chunk of the onion and several cloves of garlic into a smooth red sauce, then strain it.
Heat the olive oil in your big pot, cook the rest of the diced onion and garlic until soft, and fry the strained chile sauce in the hot oil for five minutes so it darkens and loses its raw edge.
Pour in the chicken broth along with the dried oregano, ground cumin, bay leaves, salt and black pepper, then simmer 30 minutes.
Add the drained hominy and the shredded turkey breast and simmer another 20 minutes until everything has taken on the red broth. Stir in the splash of white vinegar to brighten it.
Shred the cabbage and chop the cilantro into separate containers, cut the lime, and toast or crisp the tortillas to serve alongside.

name: Turkey Pumpkin Chili
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice separately per the package and set it aside covered.
Brown the ground turkey in your big pot over medium-high heat, breaking it up until it is cooked through.
Add the diced onion and chopped green bell peppers and cook until soft, then stir in the garlic for the last minute.
Stir in the chili powder, cocoa powder, ground cinnamon, ground cumin, cayenne, salt and black pepper and toast them against the hot pan for a minute.
Add the canned pumpkin puree, the tomato paste, the diced tomatoes with their juice and the chicken broth, and stir until the pumpkin is fully blended into the base.
Add the drained cannellini beans, simmer 30 minutes, then stir in the thawed chopped spinach at the end. Keep the sour cream and cilantro for topping at reheat.

name: Turkey Ragu Pasta
steps: Cook the penne according to the box while you get the sauce going.
Heat a little olive oil in a large skillet and brown the ground turkey.
Add the chopped onion and shredded carrots and cook until they soften.
Pour in the marinara and let it simmer 15 minutes so it turns rich and thick.
Toss the cooked penne into the sauce and stir until every noodle is coated.

name: Turkey Reuben Casserole
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cube the rye bread, toss it with the melted butter and the caraway seeds, and toast it on a sheet pan at 350F for 10 minutes until the edges dry out.
Drain the sauerkraut and squeeze it dry in a clean towel. Wring it hard, then wring it again, because kraut holds more liquid than it looks like it does.
Whisk the mayonnaise with the Dijon mustard, Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, chopped dill pickles, salt, and black pepper to make the dressing.
Spread half the toasted rye cubes across a greased 9x13 pan, then layer on the sliced turkey breast, the squeezed sauerkraut, and half the shredded Swiss.
Spoon the dressing evenly over the layers, then top with the remaining rye cubes and press the whole thing down firmly so it compacts.
Cover with foil and bake at 350F for 30 minutes, then uncover, add the rest of the Swiss, and bake 15 minutes more until browned and bubbling.
Rest 15 minutes before portioning so the layers hold together on the spatula.

name: Turkey San Choy Bow Rice Bowls
ingredients: Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 1 cups (252 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Whisk the sauce together: oyster sauce, soy sauce, chicken broth, sesame oil, and honey. Having it premixed matters, because a stir-fry does not wait for you to measure.
Dice the celery, carrot, and mushrooms small, about the size of the meat crumbles. Even dice is what makes this dish eat right instead of feeling like meat with vegetables thrown at it.
Heat a wide skillet or wok over high, add the ground turkey, and brown it hard, breaking it into fine crumbles, until it is cooked through to 165F.
Push the meat aside, add the minced garlic, grated ginger, and chopped jalapeno, and cook 30 seconds until they smell sharp and sweet.
Add the celery, carrot, and mushrooms and stir-fry 4 minutes over high heat. You want them cooked but still snapping.
Pour in the sauce and toss for 2 minutes until it reduces and coats everything, then stir in most of the sliced green onions.
Cook the rice, move it into your weighed pot, and roughly chop the peanuts for the top.

name: Turkey Sausage and Cheesy Grits Bowl
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 1 tbsp (5 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Bring the chicken broth plus enough water for your grits ratio to a boil, then whisk in the grits slowly. Drop the heat to low and simmer, stirring often, until thick and creamy, about 20 minutes.
Stir the parmesan into the grits with salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and onion powder.
While the grits cook, slice the smoked turkey sausage into coins and brown them in the olive oil with the onion until both pick up color. Add the garlic and red pepper flakes for the last minute.
Cook the eggs: bring a pot of water with the white vinegar to a bare simmer and poach the eggs 3 to 4 minutes, or fry them if that is more your speed. For meal prep, slightly firm yolks hold up best.
Build bowls: cheesy grits down, sausage and onions over the top, egg on top of that.
Reheat gently with a splash of water stirred into the grits, they tighten up in the fridge and loosen right back.

name: Turkey Sausage and Peppers Rice Skillet
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the smoked turkey sausage into coins and brown them in the olive oil in your largest deep skillet over medium-high until both cut faces are dark, then set them aside.
Add the sliced red onion and the red bell pepper strips to the same pan and cook 8 minutes, letting them pick up color from the browned bits on the bottom.
Stir in the garlic, dried oregano, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper and cook one minute until it smells like a pizzeria.
Add the dry rice and stir for two minutes so every grain gets coated in the seasoned fat. This step is what keeps the rice separate rather than sticky.
Pour in the chicken broth, return the sausage to the pan, bring it to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 18 to 20 minutes without lifting the lid.
Take the pan off the heat and let it stand covered for 10 minutes so the last of the liquid absorbs and the rice finishes steaming.
Fluff with a fork, stir in the basil pesto until it is evenly distributed, and finish with torn fresh basil.

name: Turkey Sausage and Potato Hash Skillet
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Dice the potatoes into half inch cubes and halve the Brussels sprouts, then toss everything with the olive oil, salt, and black pepper.
Spread the potatoes and sprouts across two sheet pans in a single layer. Crowding is the enemy of browning, and two pans is the difference between roasted and steamed.
Roast at 425F for 30 to 35 minutes, flipping once, until the potatoes are crisp at the corners and the sprout leaves are dark and papery.
While they roast, slice the smoked turkey sausage into coins and brown them in a large skillet over medium-high until both cut sides char.
Add the diced onion and red bell pepper to the sausage and cook 6 to 8 minutes until they soften and pick up color.
Pour the chicken broth into the skillet and scrape the bottom clean, letting it reduce down to almost nothing so the flavor stays in the pan rather than pooling.
Fold the roasted potatoes and sprouts into the skillet, taste for salt, and finish with the sliced green onions off the heat.

name: Turkey Sausage Gravy Biscuit Bake
ingredients: Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 18.25 oz (514 g)
Brown Gravy Mix (generic dry (USDA)): 12.5 oz (355 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Brown the ground turkey in a large skillet over medium-high, breaking it into small crumbles and seasoning it heavily with salt and black pepper so it reads like breakfast sausage.
Cube the sandwich bread into roughly one inch pieces and spread them across a greased and buttered 9x13 pan.
Scatter the browned turkey and about two thirds of the shredded cheddar over the bread cubes and toss lightly so it is not all sitting on top.
Whisk the eggs with about half the milk, a good pinch of salt, and plenty of black pepper, then pour the custard over the pan and press the bread down so every cube gets wet.
Whisk the gravy mix into the remaining milk in a saucepan and cook over medium heat until it thickens, then stir in the melted butter and a heavy hand of black pepper.
Pour the gravy evenly over the top of the pan. Let the whole thing sit 20 minutes so the bread finishes absorbing, or refrigerate it overnight and bake it in the morning.
Bake at 350F for 45 to 50 minutes until the center is set, adding the rest of the cheddar for the last 10 minutes, then rest 15 minutes before portioning.

name: Turkey Sausage Hash Brown Breakfast Bake
ingredients: Frozen Hash Browns (Great Value): 34 cups (2851 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 15 oz (422 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet and brown the sliced smoked turkey sausage until the edges char in spots, then set it aside. Those browned edges are the whole flavor of the dish.
In the same skillet, cook the diced onion and red bell pepper for 5 minutes until soft, then combine them with the sausage.
Spread the frozen hash browns across the bottom of a greased 9x13 pan and season them with the garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper.
Scatter the sausage and vegetable mixture over the hash browns, then cover the whole thing with about two thirds of the shredded cheddar.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, a good pinch of salt, and black pepper until completely uniform, then pour the custard evenly over the pan so it soaks down through the layers.
Bake at 375F for 45 to 55 minutes, until the center is set and does not jiggle when you nudge the pan. Add the rest of the cheddar in the last 10 minutes.
Rest 15 minutes before portioning. Egg bakes finish setting as they cool and cut far more cleanly once they do.

name: Turkey Sausage, Kale and White Bean Soup
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 0.25 tbsp (1 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice separately per the package and set it aside covered. It goes under the soup, not in the pot.
Slice the smoked turkey sausage into coins and brown them in olive oil in your big pot over medium-high heat until the edges catch color.
Drop the heat, add the minced garlic and the red pepper flakes, and stir for about a minute until it smells like an Italian kitchen.
Pour in the chicken broth and scrape the browned bits off the bottom, then bring it to a simmer.
Add the drained cannellini beans and mash a scoop of them against the side of the pot to thicken the broth.
Stir in the kale and simmer until it goes tender and dark, about 10 minutes, then season with salt and black pepper.

name: Turkey Singapore Curry Noodles
ingredients: Rice Noodles (Thai Kitchen): 55.5 oz dry (1572 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Soak the rice noodles in hot water until they are just pliable, about 8 minutes, then drain them well. They should still be firm, because they finish cooking in the pan.
Beat the eggs, scramble them in a hot oiled pan until just set, and slide them out onto a plate to add back at the end.
Brown the ground turkey in the same pan over high heat, breaking it into crumbles, until it is cooked through to 165F, then set it aside with the eggs.
Add the sliced onion, sliced red bell pepper, minced garlic, grated ginger, and chopped jalapeno, and stir-fry 4 minutes until the peppers soften but still snap.
Sprinkle the curry powder and turmeric directly into the hot pan and stir for 30 seconds until it smells toasty. Dry spice in hot oil is what makes these noodles taste like the takeout version.
Add the drained noodles and the soy sauce and toss with tongs for 3 minutes until every strand is coated gold and heated through.
Fold the turkey and egg back in, kill the heat, and stir in the green onions and most of the cilantro before moving everything into your weighed pot.

name: Turkey Sloppy Joe Bowls
ingredients: Honey Dijon Mustard (Great Value): 1 bottle (40 g)
Soy Sauce (generic): 1 tbsp (or 2 tbsp coconut aminos) (90 g)
Apple Cider Vinegar (Great Value): 1 tbsp (45 g)
steps: Bake the fries according to the bag while you get the meat going.
Brown the ground turkey in a large skillet, then add the chopped onion, peppers, and shredded carrots.
Stir in the tomato paste, honey, and honey Dijon mustard to build that sweet-tangy sloppy joe sauce.
Add a splash of water if it gets too thick and simmer until the veggies are tender.
Spoon the sloppy joe mix right over the baked fries and dig in.

name: Turkey Soboro Don
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Mix the sauce first: soy sauce, mirin, sugar, chicken broth, and grated ginger, whisked together. Split it into two bowls, a larger share for the turkey and a smaller one for the eggs.
Heat a little of the olive oil in a wide skillet, add the ground turkey, and break it apart into fine crumbles as it cooks. Fine is the goal, so keep chopping at it with your spoon.
Pour the larger share of sauce over the turkey and simmer, stirring often, until the liquid cooks down and glazes the meat and it has reached 165F. Move it to a bowl.
Wipe the skillet, add the rest of the oil, and beat the eggs with the smaller share of sauce.

Cook the eggs over medium-low, stirring constantly with chopsticks or a fork, until they set into small soft curds. Pull them the moment they stop looking wet, since they will keep cooking in the pan.
Cook the rice and move it into your weighed pot.
Slice the green onions thin and keep them separate for topping.

name: Turkey Sopa de Fideo Skillet
ingredients: Chipotle in Adobo (La Costena): 5 tbsp (84 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Break the spaghetti into pieces about an inch long. This takes a few minutes and it is what makes the dish fideo instead of just pasta.

Heat the olive oil in your largest pot over medium and toast the broken pasta, stirring constantly, for 6 to 8 minutes until it turns golden brown. Do not walk away; it goes from toasted to burnt in under a minute.
Scoop the toasted pasta out and set it aside, then blend the canned diced tomatoes with the onion, garlic, and chipotles in adobo until smooth.
Pour the blended sauce into the hot pot and fry it for 5 minutes, stirring, until it darkens and thickens. Frying the sauce is the step most people skip and it is the one that matters.
Add the chicken broth, the dried oregano, the brown sugar, salt, and black pepper, then bring it to a boil.
Return the toasted pasta to the pot, drop to a simmer, and cook uncovered 12 to 15 minutes until the noodles are tender and most of the liquid is gone.
Fold in the chopped turkey breast, warm it through for 3 minutes, and let the pot stand 10 minutes so the noodles absorb the last of the sauce.

name: Turkey Spinach Artichoke Wild Rice Casserole
ingredients: Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 28 oz (791 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Rinse the wild rice and simmer it in salted water for 40 to 45 minutes until the grains split and are tender but still chewy, then drain it well.
Brown the ground turkey in a large pot over medium-high heat, seasoning it with the Italian seasoning, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper as it cooks.
Thaw the frozen chopped spinach and wring it dry in a clean towel. Then wring it again, because this is the step that decides whether the casserole sets or slumps.
Whisk the flour into the cold milk in a jar until smooth, pour it into the pot with the turkey, and cook 5 minutes until it thickens into a sauce.
Off the heat, melt in about two thirds of the shredded mozzarella, then fold in the squeezed spinach, the drained chopped artichoke hearts, and the cooked wild rice.
Spread everything into a greased 9x13 pan and cover with the remaining mozzarella.
Bake at 375F for 30 minutes until bubbling and browned at the edges, then rest 10 minutes before portioning.

name: Turkey Stuffed Pepper Soup
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice separately per the package and set it aside. Cooking it in the soup turns the whole pot to mush by day three.
Brown the ground turkey in the olive oil in your big pot over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it goes, until no pink is left.
Add the diced onion and the chopped green bell peppers and cook until they soften, then stir in the garlic for the last minute.
Pour in the beef broth, the diced tomatoes with their juice, the tomato sauce and the Worcestershire sauce.
Add the bay leaves, dried oregano and dried thyme, bring it to a simmer, and let it go for 25 to 30 minutes so the peppers go tender and the flavors settle.
Fish out the bay leaves, season with salt and black pepper, and stir the grated parmesan in off the heat.

name: Turkey Taco Casserole
ingredients: Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 4.7 cans (1190 g)
Mexican Cheese Blend (Great Value): 23.25 oz (659 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet and brown the ground turkey, breaking it into crumbles, then season it heavily with the taco seasoning, salt, and black pepper.
Stir in the drained black beans and the salsa and simmer 10 minutes until the mixture thickens and stops running on the spoon.
Spread a thin layer of the filling in the bottom of a greased 9x13 pan so the first tortillas do not stick, then cover it with a layer of corn tortillas, overlapping like shingles.
Build three full layers: filling, tortillas, cheese, and repeat, finishing with cheese on top. Press each layer down as you go so the casserole holds together when you cut it.
Cover with foil and bake at 375F for 30 minutes, then uncover and bake 12 to 15 minutes more until the top is browned and bubbling.
Rest 20 minutes. Layered casseroles need that time or the first slice will slide apart on the spatula.
Top with the drained diced tomatoes, sliced olives, green onions, red onion, diced bell peppers, jalapenos, cilantro, and light sour cream just before portioning.

name: Turkey Taco Soup
ingredients: Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 2 cans (866 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice separately per the package and set it aside covered.
Brown the ground turkey in the vegetable oil in your big pot over medium-high heat, breaking it up until it is cooked through.
Stir in the taco seasoning, onion powder, salt and black pepper and let them toast against the hot pan for a minute.
Pour in the tomato sauce and the chicken broth and bring it to a simmer.
Add the drained kidney beans and the drained sweet corn along with the touch of sugar-free maple syrup, which balances the acid in the tomato.
Simmer 20 minutes so the flavors settle, then taste and adjust the salt. Keep the sour cream on the side.

name: Turkey Tamale Pie
ingredients: Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 10.25 oz (289 g)
Mexican Cheese Blend (Great Value): 14 oz (396 g)
Enchilada Sauce (Old El Paso): 1.7 cans (495 g)
Brown Gravy Mix (generic dry (USDA)): 1.75 oz (52 g)
Diced Green Chiles (Old El Paso): 1.8 cans (198 g)
Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 1.2 cans (301 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Warm the chopped turkey breast in a large skillet with the enchilada sauce, the drained green chiles, the drained black beans, and the chili powder, cumin, paprika, and garlic powder.
Whisk the dry gravy mix into a splash of water and stir it into the filling, then simmer 5 minutes until it thickens enough that a spoon leaves a clean line through it.
Spread the filling into a greased 9x13 pan and press it level, then scatter about half the Mexican cheese blend over it.
In a bowl, whisk the grits, flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt together, then stir in the milk, melted butter, and eggs just until the batter comes together.
Fold the drained corn and the rest of the cheese into the batter. Lumps are welcome here; overmixed cornbread bakes tight and dry.
Spoon the batter over the filling and spread it to the edges so it seals the pan completely, then bake at 400F for 30 to 35 minutes until the top is golden and set.
Rest 15 minutes, then scatter the sliced green onions over the top before portioning.

name: Turkey Tater Tot Hotdish
ingredients: Cream of Mushroom Soup (Campbell's (USDA SR)): 3 cans (876 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 11.75 oz (332 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high and brown the ground turkey, breaking it into small crumbles as it cooks.
Add the diced onion and the garlic, cook 5 minutes until the onion turns soft and translucent, then season with salt, black pepper, and smoked paprika.
Turn off the heat and stir in all three cans of condensed cream of mushroom soup along with about half the shredded cheddar. Do not thin it with water; the tots release moisture as they bake.
Spread the turkey mixture into a greased 9x13 pan and press it flat so the tot layer sits level.
Arrange the tater tots over the top in tight rows, edge to edge. A packed layer bakes into a crust; a scattered one just steams.
Bake at 400F for 40 to 45 minutes, until the tots are deep golden and the edges of the pan are bubbling.
Scatter the rest of the cheddar over the tots, return the pan for 5 minutes to melt it, then rest 10 minutes before portioning.

name: Turkey Tetrazzini
ingredients: 1/3 Fat Cream Cheese (Great Value): 14 oz (397 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 14 oz (396 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the spaghetti in salted water two minutes short of the box time, then drain it. It will finish cooking in the sauce, and mushy tetrazzini is a sad thing.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat, add the diced onion and sliced mushrooms, and cook 8 to 10 minutes until the mushrooms give up their water and it cooks back off.
Add the garlic and cook one minute, then sprinkle the flour over everything and stir for two minutes so the raw flour taste cooks out.
Pour in the chicken broth a little at a time, whisking, then add the cream cheese in chunks and the heavy cream. Stir until the sauce is smooth and thick enough to coat a spoon.
Season with salt, black pepper, and Italian seasoning, then fold in the diced turkey breast and the drained spaghetti until every strand is coated.
Spread everything into a greased 9x13 pan and cover the top with the shredded mozzarella and the parmesan.
Bake at 375F for 25 to 30 minutes, until the cheese is browned in spots and the edges bubble, then rest 10 minutes before portioning.

name: Turkey Tsukune Meatball Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Make the tare glaze first: simmer the soy sauce, mirin, brown sugar, rice vinegar, chicken broth, and some of the garlic and ginger for 10 minutes until it thickens slightly, then stir in the cornstarch slurried with a splash of cold water to finish it glossy.
Mix the ground turkey with the bread crumbs, eggs, sesame oil, the rest of the minced garlic and grated ginger, most of the sliced green onions, salt, and black pepper.
Wet your hands and roll the mixture into meatballs. Wet hands are the trick here, since this mix is soft on purpose and that softness is what makes tsukune tender.
Set them on lined sheet pans and bake at 400F for 18 to 20 minutes, until browned and cooked through to 165F.
Toss the hot meatballs in about two thirds of the glaze while they are still warm enough to drink it in, and save the rest for the containers.
Cook the rice and move it into your weighed pot.
Slice the remaining green onions and set them out with the toasted sesame seeds for topping.

name: Turkey and White Bean Cassoulet
ingredients: Hickory Smoked Bacon (Great Value): 0.25 lb (99 g)
Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 0.25 tbsp (1 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice separately per the package and set it aside. It goes under the cassoulet in the containers.
Brown the sliced smoked turkey sausage and the chopped bacon in the olive oil in a heavy oven-safe pot, then set the meat aside and leave the fat.
Cook the diced onion and sliced carrots in that fat until soft, then stir in the minced garlic, Italian seasoning, dried thyme and red pepper flakes.
Add the diced tomatoes with their juice, the drained cannellini beans, the browned sausage and bacon, and the shredded turkey breast. Season with salt and black pepper.
Bring it to a simmer on the stove, cover, and bake at 325F for about 90 minutes.
Uncover for the last 30 minutes so a crust forms on top, breaking that crust and stirring it under once or twice as it bakes.

name: Turkey Wild Rice Casserole
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Rinse the wild rice and simmer it in salted water for 40 to 45 minutes, until the grains split open and are tender but still chewy, then drain well.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat and cook the diced onion, sliced celery, and sliced mushrooms for 10 minutes, until the mushroom liquid cooks away.
Add the garlic and cook one minute, then stir in the chicken broth, milk, and heavy cream and bring it to a low simmer.
Season with the garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, salt, black pepper, and a small pinch of nutmeg, then melt in the shredded Swiss until the sauce is smooth.
Fold in the cooked wild rice and the diced turkey breast, checking that the mixture is loose. Wild rice keeps drinking liquid in the oven, so a little extra broth here is insurance.
Spread it into a greased 9x13 pan, top with the parmesan, and bake at 350F for 30 to 35 minutes until bubbling and browned at the edges.
Rest 10 minutes before portioning so the sauce tightens up around the rice.

name: Turkey Zha Jiang Mian (Beijing Noodles)
ingredients: Lo Mein Noodles (Simply Asia): 36.5 oz dry (1034 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Prep the toppings first and refrigerate them: cut the cucumber and carrot into thin matchsticks. They go on cold, so getting them out of the way early is the smart order.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or heavy skillet, add the grated ginger, minced garlic, and the white parts of the green onions, and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the ground turkey and brown it hard, breaking it into fine crumbles, until it is cooked through to 165F and starting to catch on the pan.
Add the hoisin sauce and soy sauce and fry them with the meat for 3 to 4 minutes. This frying step is what the dish is named for, and it is where the sauce loses its raw edge and turns glossy.
Pour in the chicken broth with a pinch of sugar, cinnamon, black pepper, and the bay leaves, then simmer 20 minutes until the sauce is thick enough to coat a spoon.
Boil the lo mein noodles just to the firm side of done, drain them, and rinse them under cold water so they do not keep cooking and clump in the containers.
Move the noodles into your weighed pot and toss them with a small spoon of oil so they stay loose.

name: Turkish Iskender Turkey Bowls
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 0.25 tbsp (2 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the flatbread into bite-sized squares, spread them on a sheet pan, and toast at 375F for 8 to 10 minutes until dry and lightly golden. They need to be dry enough to hold up under sauce.
Char the green peppers whole under the broiler for 8 to 10 minutes, turning once, until the skins blister, then slice them into strips.

Heat most of the olive oil in a large skillet and cook the sliced onion for 6 minutes, then add the tomato paste, paprika, red pepper flakes, salt, and black pepper and cook two minutes until the paste darkens.
Add the canned diced tomatoes and simmer 20 to 25 minutes until the sauce reduces and thickens enough to hold its shape on a spoon.
Sear the sliced turkey breast in the remaining olive oil over high heat in batches, just long enough to get color on the edges without drying it out.
Whisk the Greek yogurt smooth with a pinch of salt and a splash of water so it pours rather than sits in a lump.

Build the bowls: toasted bread cubes on the bottom, seared turkey over them, tomato sauce spooned across, melted butter drizzled over the top, charred peppers on the side, and the yogurt in its own corner.

name: Turkish Pasta with Garlic Yogurt and Spiced Butter
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 1 tbsp (6 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the penne in well salted water to al dente, drain, and toss it with a little of the olive oil so it does not stick.
Heat the rest of the olive oil in a large pot and cook the diced yellow onions until softened.
Add most of the garlic, then the ground beef, and cook until browned with no pink remaining.
Stir in the tomato paste, ground cumin, paprika, dried oregano, red pepper flakes, salt, and black pepper and cook until the paste darkens.
Add the crushed tomatoes and simmer uncovered until the sauce is thick and no longer watery.
Stir the remaining garlic and the lemon juice into the greek yogurt with a pinch of salt, and keep it cold.
Melt the butter with a spoonful of paprika until it foams and turns red, then chop the fresh mint for the finish.

name: Tuscan White Bean and Sausage Soup
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Dice the onion, carrots, celery and potatoes, mince the garlic, and strip the kale leaves off their stems.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot and brown the hot Italian sausage, breaking it into crumbles, until it has real color on it.
Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook until softened, then add the garlic, italian seasoning, dried thyme and oregano for a minute.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook it for two minutes so it darkens, then add the diced tomatoes, the chicken broth and the bay leaves.
Add the cubed potatoes and simmer until they are tender and the broth has picked up their starch.
Stir in the drained cannellini beans and cook long enough for them to warm through and start softening the broth.
Fold in the kale at the very end and cook just until it wilts, then pull the bay leaves and season with salt and black pepper.

name: Unstuffed Cabbage Roll Bowls
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 1/2 tsp (3 g)
steps: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it up as it goes, then drain the grease.
Add the chopped onion and garlic and cook until they soften.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes and the chopped cabbage, then cover and simmer until the cabbage wilts down, about 15 minutes.
Fold in the cooked rice and let it warm through so it soaks up the sauce.
Taste, adjust the salt and pepper, and serve it up in bowls.

name: Unstuffed Pepper Skillet Bowls
ingredients: Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 1 bag (170 g)
steps: Brown 4.9 pounds of 93/7 ground beef with the chopped onion and green bell peppers, then drain.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, beef broth, garlic, and italian seasoning.
Cook the rice separately, or simmer it right in the skillet with the broth until tender.
Let everything simmer together so the rice soaks up the tomato and pepper flavor.
Melt the reduced-fat mozzarella over the top before you portion it out.

name: Vietnamese Bo Kho (Lemongrass Beef Stew)
ingredients: Chili Crisp (Lao Gan Ma (Laoganma)): 5.25 tbsp (74 g)
Rice Noodles (Thai Kitchen): 24.75 oz dry (700 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Cut the chuck into large cubes and marinate it with the garlic, ginger, lemongrass paste, fish sauce, five-spice powder, brown sugar, and black pepper for at least 30 minutes. Overnight is better if you can plan that far ahead.
Heat the vegetable oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef in batches. Set it aside and keep the marinade.
Cook the sliced onion in the same pot until soft, then stir in the achiote paste, tomato paste, chili powder, and paprika and cook for a minute until the oil goes orange.
Return the beef with the remaining marinade, the chicken broth, soy sauce, and bay leaves. Add water until the meat is just covered and bring it to a simmer.
Cover and cook low for about 2 hours, then add the carrots in thick chunks and simmer uncovered another 30 minutes until they are tender and the broth has body.
Stir in the chili crisp, taste for salt and fish sauce, and pull it off the heat.
Cook the rice noodles just to tender, rinse them cold, and portion them into the containers before ladling the stew over. Top with cilantro and torn basil.

name: Vietnamese Caramelized Ground Beef Rice Bowls
ingredients: Apple Cider Vinegar (Great Value): 0.75 cups (158 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice per the package and set it aside.
Prep the fresh toppings: slice the cucumbers, halve the cherry tomatoes, shred the carrots, and thinly slice the red onion and green onions.
Heat the vegetable oil in your largest skillet over high heat and brown the ground beef hard, breaking it up, until cooked through with crispy edges.
Add the garlic, jalapeno, and lemongrass paste and stir fry 1 minute.
Add the brown sugar, fish sauce, soy sauce, and the splash of chicken broth. Cook, stirring, until the sugar melts into a dark, glossy caramel that coats the beef, 3 to 5 minutes.
Fold in most of the green onions and pull it off the heat.
Build bowls: rice, caramelized beef, then the fresh vegetables on top with a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds.

name: Vietnamese Chicken Curry (Ca Ri Ga)
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 3 lb (1400 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chicken thighs into large chunks and toss them with the ground turmeric, lemongrass paste, minced garlic, salt and black pepper. Let them sit at least 30 minutes.
Heat the vegetable oil in your largest pot over medium-high and brown the marinated chicken in batches until the turmeric has gone from yellow to gold, then set it aside.
Cook the sliced onion in the same pot for 5 minutes, scraping the bottom, then return the chicken and pour in the chicken broth.
Bring it up to a simmer and cook covered for 20 minutes so the chicken starts to give.
Add the potato and sweet potato in large chunks and simmer another 15 to 20 minutes, uncovered, until they are just fork tender. Do not stir hard or they will fall apart on you.
Break the curry roux into pieces and stir it in until it dissolves and the broth thickens, then add the coconut milk and the sugar and bring it back to a bare simmer for 5 minutes.
Taste it and adjust the salt. It should be lightly sweet, coconut-forward and thinner than an Indian curry, because that is what ca ri ga is.

name: Vietnamese Ginger Chicken (Ga Kho Gung)
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 5.25 lb (2333 g)
Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 4.75 tbsp (84 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chicken thighs into large bite-size pieces and toss them with the minced garlic, a spoonful of the fish sauce, black pepper and salt. Let them sit 20 minutes.
Slice the fresh ginger into thin matchsticks. This takes a few minutes and it is the difference between a ginger dish and a dish with ginger in it, so do not shortcut it with a grater.
Heat the vegetable oil in your largest heavy pot over medium-high and cook about a third of the ginger for 2 minutes until it smells sharp and the edges curl.
Add the honey and let it bubble and darken for a minute or two into a loose caramel. Watch it, because honey burns faster than sugar does.
Add the chicken and turn it hard in the caramel until every piece is coated and starting to brown, about 6 to 8 minutes.

Stir in the oyster sauce, the rest of the fish sauce, the chicken broth and the remaining ginger. Bring it to a simmer, then cook uncovered 25 to 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce reduces down to a thick glaze that coats the chicken.
Cook the rice separately, let it steam covered for 10 minutes, and fold it into the pot so the caramel sauce reaches every grain.

name: Vietnamese Lemongrass Chicken Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 7.75 lb (3500 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Whisk most of the fish sauce with the lemongrass paste, garlic, honey, soy sauce, black pepper, and a little sugar into a marinade. Hold back some fish sauce, sugar, lime juice, and the jalapeno for the sauce.
Toss the chicken thighs in the marinade and refrigerate at least 2 hours. Overnight is better and this is one of the few recipes where that really shows.

Make the nuoc cham by stirring the reserved fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, and warm water together until the sugar dissolves, then add the minced jalapeno. Taste it. It should be sharp, salty, and sweet all at once.

Heat the oven to 425F, lay the chicken on a sheet pan in a single layer, and roast 25 to 30 minutes until the edges char. Crowding the pan steams the chicken and you lose the caramelization entirely, so use two pans if you have to.
Cook the rice while the chicken roasts.
Rest the chicken 5 minutes, then slice it across the grain and toss it with any juices left on the pan.
Shred the carrots, slice the cucumber thin, and chop the cilantro.

name: Vietnamese Lemongrass Pork Chops with Broken Rice (Com Suon)
ingredients: Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 4.5 oz (126 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Whisk the marinade: lemongrass paste, garlic, fish sauce, soy sauce, oyster sauce, honey, brown sugar, half the vegetable oil, and the grated onion. Coat the pork chops and marinate at least 30 minutes, overnight is better.
Cook the rice per the package and set it aside.
Sear the chops in a ripping hot pan or grill them, a few at a time, letting the sugars char at the edges. Cook to 145F and rest 5 minutes before slicing.
Simmer the leftover marinade in the pan drippings for a few minutes at a full boil to make a safe, glossy drizzle sauce.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil, one per serving, leaving the yolks as soft or firm as your meal prep nerves allow.
Slice the cucumbers and drain the diced tomatoes for the fresh side.
Build bowls: rice, sliced pork, egg on top, cucumber and tomato beside, sauce and green onions over everything.

name: Vietnamese Lemongrass Pork Noodle Bowls (Bun Thit Nuong)
ingredients: Rice Noodles (Thai Kitchen): 24.75 oz dry (700 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the pork loin into thin strips. Marinate it in about a third of the fish sauce and a third of the sugar for at least 20 minutes.

Make the nuoc cham dressing: stir the remaining fish sauce and sugar with the lime juice and about 2 cups of warm water until the sugar dissolves. Taste it, it should hit sweet, salty, and sour in that order.
Cook the rice noodles per the package, drain, and rinse under cold water. These bowls are meant to be eaten cool or room temperature.
Sear the pork in a very hot pan in batches, letting it char at the edges, until cooked through to 145F.
Slice the cucumbers, shred the carrots, and rough-chop the mint and cilantro.
Build bowls: noodles down, pork on top, vegetables and herbs around it, peanuts over everything. Pack the nuoc cham separately and pour it on when you eat.

name: Vietnamese Thit Kho Braised Pork and Eggs
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the pork shoulder into large chunks and slice the onion. Hard boil the eggs, cool them and peel them.
Melt the sugar in a heavy pot over medium heat without stirring and let it turn a deep amber caramel. Watch it closely, because caramel goes from amber to burnt in about ten seconds.
Add the pork chunks to the caramel and stir to coat every piece, then add the sliced onion.
Pour in the fish sauce and the soda, which will hiss and seize the caramel at first. Keep stirring and it will loosen back out.
Add enough water to nearly cover the pork, bring it to a simmer, and skim off whatever foam rises in the first few minutes.
Cover and braise very low until the pork is tender and the liquid has reduced into a glossy sauce, stirring occasionally.
Add the peeled eggs for the last stretch so they take on color and flavor, season with salt and black pepper, and cook the rice separately.

name: Vietnamese Turkey Banh Mi Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice per the package and set it aside.
Quick-pickle the vegetables: shred the carrots and slice a third of the cucumbers thin, then toss with the rice vinegar and sugar. Let them sit at least 20 minutes, stirring once or twice.
Make the sriracha mayo: stir about two thirds of the sriracha into the mayonnaise with half the lime juice.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over high heat. Brown the ground turkey, breaking it up, then add the garlic, lemongrass paste, and remaining sriracha, and cook until the turkey reaches 165F.
Stir the fish sauce and remaining lime juice into the turkey and let it sizzle 1 more minute.
Slice the remaining cucumbers fresh.
Build bowls: rice, lemongrass turkey, pickled veg, fresh cucumber, green onions, and a drizzle of sriracha mayo. Pack extra mayo separately if you like it cold.

name: Vietnamese Turkey Xiu Mai Meatballs over Rice
ingredients: Rice Noodles (Thai Kitchen): 24.75 oz dry (700 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Finely dice about a third of the onion and mix it into the ground turkey with a good portion of the minced garlic, some of the fish sauce, a spoon of the sugar, salt, and black pepper.
Roll the mixture into large meatballs, about golf ball size, and chill them 15 minutes so they hold their shape when they hit the pan.
Cook the rest of the diced onion and garlic in a wide pot until soft and fragrant, about 6 minutes. There is a lot of garlic here and that is the point of the dish.
Stir in the tomato paste and fry it for 2 minutes until it darkens, then add the diced tomatoes, the rest of the fish sauce, the sugar, and the chicken broth.
Lower the meatballs into the sauce, cover, and simmer gently for 30 minutes, turning them once, until they are cooked through to 165F and the sauce has thickened around them.
Taste the sauce and adjust with a little more sugar or fish sauce. It should be savory, faintly sweet, and unmistakably garlicky.
Soak and boil the rice noodles just to tender, rinse them cold, and move them into your weighed pot with the chopped cilantro and green onions folded through.

name: West African Jollof Rice and Chicken
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 6.5 lb (2911 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Season the chicken thighs with salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and half the curry powder and thyme.
Sear the thighs in the vegetable oil in your largest pot until browned on both sides, then set them aside. They finish cooking later.
Cook the onion and green bell pepper in the same pot until soft, then add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.

Add the tomato sauce with the smoked paprika, remaining curry powder, thyme, and cayenne, and cook it down 8 to 10 minutes until it darkens and the oil starts to separate. This step is where jollof flavor lives, do not rush it.

Stir in the rice to coat, pour in the chicken broth, and nestle the chicken on top. Cover tightly and simmer on low until the rice is tender and the chicken reads 165F, about 25 minutes. Resist stirring, the bottom crust is a feature.
Scatter the frozen peas and jalapeno over the pot, cover 3 more minutes, then fold everything together.

name: Xinjiang Cumin Beef Rice Bowls
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 1 tbsp (6 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the beef thin against the grain, then toss it with a pinch of baking soda, the soy sauce, cornstarch, and the chicken broth until every slice is slick. Let it sit 20 minutes.
Mince the ginger and garlic, slice the jalapenos, and cut the green onions into short lengths. Have all of it within arm's reach, because this cooks fast.
Heat the vegetable oil in your widest pan until it is genuinely hot, then sear the beef in batches, spread out, without stirring for the first 30 seconds.
Pull each batch out as soon as it loses its raw color. Overcrowding the pan steams the beef and steamed beef is tough.
Return the pan to high heat, add the ginger, garlic, and jalapenos, and stir for 30 seconds.
Add all the beef back with the ground cumin, red pepper flakes, salt, and pepper, and toss hard for a minute so everything coats.
Kill the heat, hit it with the sesame oil, green onions, and cilantro, and cook the rice separately.

name: Xinjiang Cumin Turkey Stir-Fry
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Slice the turkey breast into thin strips against the grain, then toss them with the baking soda and a splash of water and let them sit 20 minutes. This is velveting, and it is why restaurant stir-fry meat is tender and yours usually is not.
Rinse the turkey well, pat it dry, then toss it with the soy sauce, chicken broth, and the flour so each strip has a light coating.

Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or heavy skillet until it is nearly smoking. Sear the turkey in batches, giving each batch room, until browned and cooked through to 165F. Crowding the pan is how you steam meat by accident.
Pour off most of the oil, then toast the dried arbol chilies and the cumin for 30 seconds until the kitchen makes you cough a little. That is the correct amount.
Add the sliced onion, grated ginger, and minced garlic and stir-fry 3 minutes until the onion softens at the edges but still has structure.
Return all the turkey, add a pinch of sugar, salt, and black pepper, and toss over high heat for 2 minutes so everything gets coated in spice. It should look dry, not saucy.
Kill the heat, fold in the chopped cilantro and sesame seeds, then cook the rice and move it into your weighed pot.

name: Youvarlakia Avgolemono (Greek Beef and Rice Meatballs in Lemon Sauce)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Mix the ground beef with the dry rice, finely grated yellow onion, chopped fresh mint, salt, and black pepper until just combined.
Roll the mixture into evenly sized meatballs, keeping them a little smaller than you think, since the rice expands.
Bring a large pot of water with the olive oil and a good amount of salt to a gentle simmer.
Lower the meatballs in, cover, and simmer gently until the rice inside is fully cooked and the meatballs are firm. Do not let it boil hard or they break apart.
Lift the meatballs out with a slotted spoon and keep the cooking broth at a bare simmer.
Whisk the eggs with the lemon juice in a bowl until frothy, then ladle in hot broth a little at a time while whisking constantly. This tempering step is the whole trick.
Pour the tempered egg mixture back into the pot off the heat, stir until the broth thickens and turns pale, then return the meatballs and season to taste.

name: Zanzibar-Style One Pot Chicken Pilau
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 5 lb (2240 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Rinse the rice in cold water until the water runs clear, then leave it to soak while you cook. Rinsed rice is what keeps pilau grains separate instead of gluey.

Melt the butter in your largest heavy pot over medium heat and cook the sliced red onion for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring, until it goes past golden and into deep brown. This is where pilau gets its color, and there is no shortcut.
Add the garlic, then the ground cumin, garam masala, ground cloves, ground cinnamon, black pepper, poultry seasoning and bay leaves. Stir for a minute in the hot fat.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook it another minute until it turns brick red, then add the chicken thighs cut into chunks and turn them until coated. Cook 5 minutes.
Drain the rice and add it to the pot, folding gently so it takes on the spiced onion. Pour in the chicken broth and beef broth, season with salt, and bring it to a boil.
Drop the heat to the lowest setting, cover tightly, and cook 20 to 25 minutes without lifting the lid. Then pull it off the heat and let it sit covered another 10 minutes.
Fish out the bay leaves and fluff the whole pot with a fork, lifting from the bottom so the browned rice at the base gets distributed.

name: Zuppa Toscana (Sausage, Potato and Kale Soup)
ingredients: Hickory Smoked Bacon (Great Value): 0.25 lb (140 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Chop the bacon, dice the onion, mince the garlic, slice the potatoes into rounds and strip the kale leaves from their stems.
Render the chopped bacon in a large pot until it crisps, then lift it out and leave the fat behind.
Brown the hot Italian sausage in the bacon fat, breaking it into crumbles, until it is cooked through and browned in spots. Drain off any excess grease.
Add the diced onion and cook until soft, then add the garlic and italian seasoning for a minute.
Pour in the chicken broth, add the sliced potatoes, and simmer until they are tender enough to cut with a spoon.
Turn the heat down and stir in the heavy cream, keeping it below a boil so it does not separate.
Fold in the kale and the crisped bacon, cook just until the kale wilts, then season with salt and black pepper.
